items.claim: Server-side template injection is proven by sending an arithmetic expression such as {{7*7}}; evaluating to 49 shows the template engine evaluated attacker input.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: A backend that handles user-supplied input insecurely can lead to sensitive information disclosure and remote code execution. This module covers how to identify and exploit server-side bugs. This module introduces Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), and Server-Side Includes (SSI) injection attacks, alongside other server-side vulnerabilities.

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/05. Web Exploitation/31d. Server-side Attacks/Server-side Attacks.md (740 words, classified web).
items.disproof: Refuted when the expression is returned verbatim as literal text rather than evaluated, which shows the input is not reaching a template engine.
